capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extraction in the load()->processor path: it pads/
truncates every input to a fixed 3000-frame (30 s) mel window, and generate()
accepts a batched feature StorageView with one prompt per batch row.
what_i_learned:
The processor silently caps each call at one 30 s window, so the stub deleted
the entire tail of any recording longer than 30 s. The backend's generate()
takes a stacked (N, n_mels, 3000) feature batch plus an N-length prompt list
and returns one result per window, letting a whole long-form clip be decoded
in a single batched call rather than one truncated window.
hypothesis:
Splitting the waveform into consecutive 30 s windows and concatenating the
per-window transcripts recovers the deleted tail, which should collapse the
deletion-dominated CER far more than any decode-knob tweak on a single window.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s memory behaviour under a batched (N, n_mels, 3000) feature
StorageView vs. one-window-at-a-time calls — i.e. how peak GPU memory scales
with the number of stacked prompts in a single generate() call.
what_i_learned:
The backend's batched generate() allocates decode state for ALL N windows at
once, so a long clip (many 30 s windows stacked into one call) exhausts CUDA
memory — the failure was OOM, not a shape/contract bug. Decoding the same
windows sequentially (N separate single-row generate calls) is numerically
equivalent for the transcript but caps peak memory at one 30 s window.
hypothesis:
Keep iter_001's long-form windowing (split waveform into <=30 s chunks so the
tail is no longer deleted) but decode each chunk in its own generate() call
and join the pieces, fixing the CUDA-OOM crash while preserving the tail
coverage that motivated the change.

capability_investigated:
The decode return channel when <|notimestamps|> is omitted from the prompt:
generate()'s sequences_ids then contain Whisper timestamp tokens (the high
end of the vocab, >= the <|0.00|> id), each step = 0.02 s. The fixed-stride
pipeline suppressed and discarded these entirely.
what_i_learned:
Timestamp tokens are recoverable from results[0].sequences_ids without any
backend flag — just drop <|notimestamps|> from the prompt and read token ids
>= tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"); their value gives the time
the model attended to inside each 30 s window. Linguistic tokens are all
below that id, so text and timestamps separate cleanly by a single id cutoff.
hypothesis:
Deletion (80%, length_ratio 0.65) is driven by blind 30 s strides skipping
audio when a window's content ends early (EOT/repetition collapse before
30 s). Steering the next window's start to the model's own last timestamp
instead of seek+30 s stops skipping unread tails and should raise coverage.

capability_investigated:
The prompts argument of generate(): besides the SOT/language/task triple,
ctranslate2 Whisper accepts an arbitrary prompt token list, so the
<|startofprev|> token + prior-text tokens can prefix the decode prompt to
condition on previous output — the standard Whisper context channel.
what_i_learned:
The decode prompt is a free token list, not a fixed header: prepending
<|startofprev|> + the previous window's re-encoded text tokens (capped ~200,
no special tokens) carries cross-window context into the decoder. This is an
input channel the job has never used — every prior iter passed only the
fixed triple, so each 30 s window decoded blind to its own running transcript.
hypothesis:
Feeding the running transcript back via <|startofprev|> conditions the model
on just-said domain terminology, biasing it toward contextually-consistent
recognition. Diagnosis shows coverage is healthy (length_ratio 0.95) and the
dominant error is substitution (54%), so the lever is *what* is recognized,
not how much — prior-context conditioning attacks exactly that axis while the
timestamp-steered seek preserves coverage.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam-search decode params (beam_size, patience, length_penalty)
on the family_002 timestamp-steered window — the parent decoded greedily
(beam_size=1), never using the backend's beam path or its quality knobs.
what_i_learned:
The dominant axis is substitution (54%) with healthy coverage (length_ratio
0.95), so the lever is sequence-search quality, not windowing. Greedy commits
to the locally-best token and cannot recover a globally-better transcript
through ambiguous phone-band domain terms; a beam holds the runner-up. The
prior bare beam attempt (iter_005) returned no cer at all, consistent with a
full beam=5 (~5x) overrunning the 719.9 s budget — so beam width must be
budget-bounded, not conventional.
hypothesis:
Switch the parent's greedy decode to a small beam (beam_size=2, patience=2.0,
length_penalty=1.0). This gives the decoder one alternative to greedy
commitment on ambiguous spans — aimed straight at substitution — while
~2-2.5x runtime stays well inside budget where a full beam=5 did not.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam-search width on the family_002 timestamp-steered window —
specifically whether beam_size=2 (the parent) explores a deep enough
hypothesis set to move the substitution axis, vs whether the encoder cost
being shared across beam rows leaves budget headroom to widen it.
what_i_learned:
The parent's width-2 beam did not move substitution at all (sub 54 -> 54.6%)
and only added insertions (9 -> 13%), so a single retained runner-up is too
shallow to recover the globally-correct token on ambiguous phone-band domain
terms. The encoder features are computed once per window and shared across
the beam, so widening beam_size scales only the decode portion — at the
parent's 214 s of a 719.9 s budget, beam=4 stays comfortably inside it.
hypothesis:
Widen beam_size 2 -> 4 (patience=2.0, length_penalty=1.0 unchanged) so the
decoder holds a deeper alternative set across acoustically-ambiguous spans,
directly targeting the dominant substitution axis where the narrow beam
failed to improve over greedy.
